title: wsutil: Pull out "application flavor" to its own folder
description: Pull out the functionality of "application flavor" and put it into a separate folder, one for Wireshark (packets) and one for Stratoshark (events).  Then applications only have to like the appropriate module that they support, either packets or events.  There's no need for an explicit setting of behavior, just link to the desired module. This works towards better isolating the differences between Wireshark and Stratoshark and not having explicit checks for which application is running.

notes.body:
This is an early proof of concept.  Right now the "application libraries" have the same code just so I could provide out the creation of the library. Eventually the enumerations would go away and just be replaced with the implementation respective to the application.
Some thoughts:
1. Opinions on library/folder names?
2. Am I really linking these properly together?  I think over time refactoring should bubble up some of the "is wireshark/is stratoshark checks" so that they aren't in so many libraries to have to link to.
3. To me the "Definition of Done" for this MR is just the successful creation of the libraries, building and running on all current platforms.  Not sure I've successfully made all of the changes necessary for that to happen (but I will keep chipping away at the original patch to make sure it passes the pipeline before I work on additional suggestions that may come)

Turned off "Draft" status in case it was scaring off reviewers as they thought it may still be a "work in progress".  The functionality here is complete, but the intent is to build on it later.  To me, the "harder" part is adding this new architecture of extra libraries.  It will be easier to add content to the libraries later.
Commenting on the thoughts above:
1. Still would like opinions on library/folder names (and if there are things like trademarks we need to be concerned with)
2. In separate MRs, I worked on removing a lot of the "is wireshark/is stratoshark checks" so that functionality is now just at the UI/application layer (and it passed into the supporting dissection libraries)
3. I believe this "Definition of Done" has been achieved, but I don't have the ability to test on all supported platforms. The pipeline doesn't appear to run installers to see if all suppporting libraries are properly installed. During development, testing on Windows showed I wasn't installing the application libraries, so Wireshark wouldn't run (that's been fixed).  This MR has the potential to break Wireshark so that it doesn't run, so I want to be cautious when approving it.

This MR has the potential to break applications *for people who are living on the bleeding edge*, and those people have presumably *chosen* to do that (I hope we provide sufficient warnings that we can presume this to be an *informed* choice), so I'm not sure *too* much caution is necessary.

Wireshark as a whole is a stable application, so users trust it well enough that "living on the bleeding edge" usually means the packet dissection may be a little off or incomplete or analysis tools may not be feature complete.  That's different from (accidentally) breaking it so that it doesn't run. I don't want to lose that "free testing" trust we have in those users.
But also, I want to introduce this now so that the architecture is ironed out before the 5.0 release.

I'd prefer I we ran Debian package building test for MR-s and I think it would not take too much time, but this is up to @geraldcombs , I think.
IMO packaging changes should be handled together with other code changes and I always try include them. (For RPM, too.)

Regarding the MR itself is this really worth it?
```
$ git diff 09039dcb9a..019d1ac014  --stat | tail
 ui/qt/widgets/hex_data_source_view.cpp           |   2 +-
 ui/qt/widgets/traffic_tab.cpp                    |   2 +-
 ui/qt/wireshark_main_window_slots.cpp            |   2 +-
 ui/recent.c                                      |   2 +-
 ui/stratoshark/stratoshark_main.cpp              |  12 +-
 ui/stratoshark/stratoshark_main_window_slots.cpp |   2 +-
 wiretap/CMakeLists.txt                           |   1 +
 wsutil/CMakeLists.txt                            |   4 +-
 wsutil/application_flavor.c                      | 214 -----------------------
 105 files changed, 906 insertions(+), 348 deletions(-)
```

IMO this is way more added than removed complexity.
Also shared library names are a global namespace and we should be mindful about collisions and not reserving them without strong reason in general.

This is exactly the conversation I wanted to have with this MR.  The intention behind the "complexity" is adding future flexibility for other applications that may want this architecture, i.e. (something like) Fileshark. So, I want a piece designed to "plug in" to provide things like "name", "environment variables" and eventually things like "which dissectors should be supported" (still working on completely isolating epan and the dissector directory from the UI).
Would a static library of this functionality be better?  My CMake skills aren't great and this started as a copy/paste of the wsutil library where "application flavor" currently sits.  And that's really the only reason it's a shared library ATM.

IMO even static libraries would be overkill. IMO having two .c/.o files linked to either `wireshark`/`tshark` or `stratoshark`/`strato` should be enough to carry the differences between the tool flavors and avoid code duplication between the GUI and ClI commands. The API of the current libraries can be reworked to accept parameters such that they can work with either flavor without calling back to the new .c/.o files they would be used only by the top level applications.

My impression is that `eshark` or events handling is (and expected to be) so little code compared to the packet handling parts that it is not worth it to split it out from `libwireshark` and AFAIK there is no long term plan to make Stratoshark a separately developed project that would make the split necessary even if it is not worth it. If this is the case, I see not benefit in creating new libraries, but the downside would be the extra complexity to maintain, here, in the project, and in downstream distributions.

One of the big reasons I made this a library now was I (eventually) wanted to split libwireshark into "epan library" and "dissector library" so that "epan library" stands strictly as a dissection engine (agnostic to packet or event).  And pshark and eshark would then include the "dissector library" (technically removing libwireshark). So, the "pshark library" would be small for now but would eventually include all Wireshark dissectors.

I've tried to do make a separate "dissection library" on some private branches and there have definitely been hurdles (in how everything links).  But you can also see there have been smaller MRs that have come out of that to better separate Wireshark and Stratoshark (abstracting to a better generic dissection engine).

You're right that the new C files have basically been written, it would just be a matter of having the applications specifically calling them out instead of the (new) libraries.  Maybe that is a better "first step" for a more official separation.

commits_data.title: wsutil: Pull out "application flavor" to its own folder
commits_data.message:
wsutil: Pull out "application flavor" to its own folder

Pull out the functionality of "application flavor" and put it into a separate folder, one for Wireshark (packets) and one for Stratoshark (events).  Then applications only have to link the appropriate module that they support, either packets or events.  There's no need for an explicit setting of behavior, just link to the desired module. This works towards better isolating the differences between Wireshark and Stratoshark and not having explicit checks for which application is running.
